analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Rotation into hyperscalers and out of semis, Starlink aspirations, NEM mixed, BT beat, Swisscom OFCF raise, DT mixed, JCD beats (5 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Tech rotated sharply into hyperscalers and out of semis and datacentre infrastructure on 5 Nov 2026, as investors read the Democratic midterm win as making new datacentre builds harder and existing, power-secured compute more valuable. QQQ finished +1% after being up as much as 2.5%, SPY +1.6%, VIX down 2-3 points. Semis fell 3%, after dropping as much as 5% intraday, underperforming QQQ by 4 percentage points.

The US desk's largest thematic flow was buying hyperscalers versus selling semis, across a mix of client types, from both long-only and hedge fund clients. AMZN rose 7-8%, MSFT 4-7%, GOOGL 5-6%, META 3%, with Apple also strong. Combined Mag7-style market-value gains approached $750bn-$1tn. CoreWeave fell 7-11%, Nebius 4-6%, and other neoclouds and datacentre builders also fell. MU and memory were weaker, while NVDA was only slightly lower.

Debate on the AI datacentre buildout: the Democratic win could slow US capacity through tighter permitting, water and power rules, fewer tax breaks and temporary moratoria. Brad Gerstner argued on All-In that regulatory friction could stop 10-15 GW of expected 2027 capacity. He had already been below Street estimates at about 25 GW in September. GIR is at 20GW for the US, well below Street, and sees more risk in 2028. SemiAnalysis flagged 16.7GW of planned 2028 Texas capacity at risk. Street forecasts are well above 30GW.

The counterview on datacentre capacity is more sanguine about 2027, because most capacity is already under construction or permitted. Texas moratoria would be constrained by the legislature, and many local bans hit areas with little real activity. The desk's view is that a broad shutdown is unlikely and delays and higher costs are the real risk. GIR expects datacentre focus to fade after the midterms because it ranks low in voter priorities.

If there are short-term delays, installed and power-secured compute becomes more valuable. Hyperscalers AMZN and MSFT are seen as near-term winners. Pure new-build names (ORCL expansions, NEOS, SPCX, pure-play AI cloud) are seen as laggards.

AI and semis sceptics ask whether the semis narrative flips to an inventory correction if power and sites lag chip deliveries. They cite Microsoft's Nov 2025 comments about chips sitting idle for lack of power and space. The FT reported that AWS takes delivery of about $3bn of Nvidia GB300 racks per month and stages some in warehouses because certain sites lack power. The desk says there may be no demand issue but a near-term semis inventory issue if delays resemble the 2022-23 post-pandemic correction.
A second investor debate holds that sustained AI growth requires the cost of compute to keep falling, and that higher compute costs reduce displacement pressure on traditional software and media.
In Europe the flow was similar, with one-way long-only supply across AI names including ASML, IFX and ENR.

US telcos: SpaceX signed a deal with Qualcomm for its Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure platforms to support Starlink Mobile's terrestrial base stations. US telcos ignored the news as a safe place to hide. The desk reads it as Starlink assembling physical infrastructure to challenge Tier-1 mobile operators, with US nationwide deployment starting in 2027. It is negative for Ericsson and, to a lesser extent, Nokia.

NEM results were mixed: revenue in line, organic growth 12.5% vs street 13.6%, Design 6.5% vs street 8.5%, Build 23.6% vs street 22%, EBITDA 1% ahead, FCF conversion above 100%. Group guidance was reiterated despite lowering the Manage and Media outlooks.

DT results were mixed: group revenue and adjusted EBITDA AL beat, lower capex drove an OFCF beat, and FY guidance was raised marginally for the US. The buyback is EUR2bn vs Street EUR3bn. Germany EBITDA growth is now expected at the low end of the 2.5-3% FY26 guidance. A Handelsblatt article says DT is still pursuing a merger with T-Mobile US, despite Bloomberg reporting the process was on hold.

BT beat on revenue, EBITDA (3% ahead) and line loss (Openreach 175k vs Street 197k), but higher capex caused an OFCF miss. FY guidance was reiterated and excludes TalkTalk. The consumer market is highly competitive and H2 is expected to be the same or worse than H1. The triennial pension deficit is GBP2.7B, in line with the Street, and contributions will be substantially replaced with zero-coupon bonds, with BT adding GBP0.3B NPV of funding.

Swisscom revenue beat by 1.4% and reported EBITDAaL missed by 1.2% (a beat excluding the E39m restructuring), and OFCF beat on lower capex. OFCF guidance was raised to above CHF2.0B from around CHF2.0B.

SES beat in Q3 and reiterated FY revenue and EBITDA guidance. FY capex guidance was cut to about EUR600mn from EUR700mn vs consensus EUR706mn. Revenue was 1.3% ahead and adjusted EBITDA 12.6% ahead. The CMD was delayed from December to March.

Bouygues beat by about 1% on revenue and about 2% on COPA. Equans COPA margin guidance was raised to at least 5.5% from 5.2%, and group guidance was raised to slight growth. JCD 3Q26 organic growth was +6.6% vs company guidance of about 5%, with Digital Out-of-Home +15.3% and programmatic +37.5%. 4Q guidance is about 6% organic growth.

US overnight: QCOM fell 7.5% after hours on weaker earnings and margin guidance despite in-line revenue and better December-quarter revenue guidance. GIR cut QCOM estimates by 8% on average. QCOM expects the smartphone market to decline in the low-to-mid teens in CY26. ARM was down 1.7% after hours on a royalty revenue miss despite above-Street guidance. COHR rose 7.6% with FY27 pro forma growth above 60%.

HUBS beat Q3 but guided Q4 growth to 12% vs the roughly 14.5-15% expected, which management attributed to AI changing how customers find and buy software, and revived the AI-at-risk debate. APP rose 20% after its biggest revenue beat since Q4 2025, guidance well above expectations and a $3.2bn buyback. SNAP had mixed Q3 results with advertising growth slowing to low-to-mid single digits and about 30 million paid subscribers.

earnings_insights: NEM (reported 5 Nov): revenue in line, organic growth 12.5% vs street 13.6%, Design 6.5% vs street 8.5%, Build 23.6% vs street 22%, EBITDA 1% ahead, FCF conversion above 100%. Group guidance reiterated.

SINCH (reported 5 Nov): top line, organic gross profit growth (about 4% y/y ex-fx) and EBITDA broadly in line. FCF EUR967mn vs consensus, significantly stronger. Americas organic gross profit grew about 10%, and APAC organic gross profit was -10%, ahead of expectations.
NEXI (reported 5 Nov): revenue +1.4% vs street 1.5%, Merchant Services +1.7%, EBITDA 2% ahead, guidance reiterated.

DT (reported 5 Nov): group revenue and adjusted EBITDA AL beat, Germany service revenue 0.4% ahead, lower capex drove an OFCF beat. FY guidance raised marginally for the US. Germany EBITDA growth +1.5% y/y in 3Q26, needs at least +3.5% in 4Q26 vs consensus just over 4%. Buyback EUR2bn vs Street EUR3bn. DT guides to about EUR11bn vs consensus EUR10.98bn.

BT (reported 5 Nov): service revenue (0.6%), EBITDA (3% ahead) and line loss beat, OFCF missed on higher capex. FY guidance reiterated and excludes TalkTalk. Triennial pension deficit GBP2.7B in line with street.

Swisscom (reported 5 Nov): revenue beat by 1.4%, reported EBITDAaL missed by 1.2% (beat excluding the E39m restructuring), OFCF beat on lower capex. OFCF guidance raised to above CHF2.0B from around CHF2.0B.
SES (reported 5 Nov): revenue 1.3% ahead of consensus, adjusted EBITDA 12.6% ahead. FY capex guidance about EUR600mn vs EUR700mn previously and consensus EUR706mn.
Bouygues (reported 5 Nov): about 1% beat on revenue and about 2% beat on COPA. Equans COPA margin guidance raised from 5.2% to at least 5.5%. Group guidance raised to slight growth.
JCD (reported 5 Nov): 3Q26 organic growth +6.6% vs company guidance of about 5% and above consensus. Digital Out-of-Home +15.3%, programmatic +37.5%. 4Q guidance about 6% organic growth.
AUTO LN (reported 5 Nov): H1 revenue about 2% below expectations, mostly on weaker vehicle and accessory sales, EBIT better, FY27 guidance reiterated.

QCOM (reported after the close 4 Nov): revenue in line, December-quarter revenue guidance slightly better than expected, earnings and margin guidance below expectations. GIR cut estimates by 8% on average. Smartphone market expected to decline in the low-to-mid teens in CY26 and be flat to down slightly in CY27.

ARM (reported after the close 4 Nov): revenue and EPS guidance above Street expectations, royalty revenue missed, licensing strong with four new CSS customers. Management has greater confidence in $2bn of AGI CPU revenue in FY27-28.

COHR (reported 4 Nov after the close): in line quarter, gross margin missed by about 10-30bps, FY27 pro forma growth above 60%, implying above about $11.2B on the about $7.0B FY26 base vs Street $10.63B.

HUBS (reported 4 Nov after the close): Q3 revenue +17% in constant currency vs expectations of about 15.5-16%. Q4 growth guidance 12% vs about 14.5-15% expected. Full-year net revenue retention expected to fall about 2 pp, net new ARR to decline y/y, Q4 net customer additions below 5,000.
APP (reported 4 Nov after the close): biggest revenue beat since Q4 2025, core gaming growth of nearly 50% y/y, guidance well above expectations, $3.2bn buyback, trades at 15x P/E.
SNAP (reported 4 Nov after the close): Q3 2026 total revenue grew mid-teens y/y, broadly in line, advertising growth slowed to low-to-mid single digits, about 30 million paid subscribers.
